findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Ranch dressing labeled "keep refrigerated" is 47°F internal and 57-58 along edge. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F ranch was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

A gallon and a half of ranch was voluntarily discarded.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
At 12:30pm, a pan of cooked chicken was found in the pass-thru warmer unit at 122 degrees F.  CORRECTED - It was determined that chicken was greater than 135 approximately 1 hour prior.  Staff intended to rapidly cool chicken for later use.  Rapid cooling began, and food will be below 70 degrees F by 1:30pm.  Proper rapid cooling discussed.  See HACCP topic.

750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from >135 to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
4 oz cartons of apple juice (stamped "Keep Refrigerated") were on display in cardboard boxes at room temperature, next to the "check out" computer.  Apple juice cartons were being blown with hot air from computer and found at temperatures of 38 - 60 degrees F (laser).  IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED - cartons that were still at proper cold holding temperature were immediately placed back into walk-in cooler.  Juice that was above proper temperature was passed out to children, or discarded, by 3pm (~ four hours from time of removal from cold holding).  Discussed this practice with Aramark director and Kitchen Lead.  Juice will be dispensed to children in cooler, with the milk, or placed in ice baths, to protect proper cold holding temperatures.  Also, closely monitor milk temperatures, as their coolers are opened for self-service during lunch period.  Make sure milk cartons (as well as juice) remain at 41 degrees or below.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
At approximately 11:15, eggs and tater tots in hot holding cabinets were found at temperatures 100 - 110 degrees F (laser).  The foods on the right side of the cabinet appeared to be at proper temperatures, however, the foods on the left side appear to be below 135.  Later, Aramark manager and inspector took probe-thermometer-temperatures of pan of eggs and got temperatures of 100 degrees F and 143 degrees F.  Both thermometers were properly calibrated.  Eggs were stirred, and more temperatures taken, resulting in temperatures of ~120 degrees F.  Temp logs show eggs were 187 degrees at 10am.  IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED - as 2.5 hrs had lapsed, in interest of safety, eggs were voluntarily discarded.  Four cheeseburgers at 90 degrees F and I tray of tater tots (at 108 - 110 F) were also voluntarily discarded from hot holding.  This particular cabinet has four doors, and closing one door frequently causes another to pop open.  It is possible a door was open, causing unit to lose heat on the left side.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)
